newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHANG BREEZES INTO OPEN SECOND ROUND. [CORRECTED 2:18 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG BREEZES INTO OPEN SECOND ROUND. [CORRECTED 2:18 GMT]

text.p: World number two Michael Chang, seeking his first grand slam title in eight years, breezed into the second round of the Australian Open on Monday with a straight-sets win over Belgian qualifier Kris Goossens.

Chang, showing the form that catapulted him into the final of last year's Open without losing a set, took one hour and 35 minutes to dispatch Goossens 6-0 6-3 6-1 in blustery conditions on court two at Melbourne Park.
Goossens, ranked 132 in the world, barely made an impression on Chang, despite the American second seed making a string of early unforced errors before finding his rhythm.
Chang, who won the French Open as a raw 17-year-old (Corrects)
in 1989 but lost to Boris Becker in Melbourne last year, produced a typically relentless performance as he settled into the match.
Chang, will next meet the winner of the first round match between American Richey Reneberg, ranked 32 in the world, and Spanish qualifier Oscar Burrieza.
